scope: The NULL cell, re-measured at this tip on the real RTX 5090 through the GPU queue. The SAME empty binary is run twice and treated as (scale, empty): a null cell cannot be faster than itself, so any negative kernel_us there is the estimator's own noise. Reported per estimator over 20 repeats: how many readings are negative. No admission-threshold change and no kernel_us clamping is claimed.

substituted_input.declared: The provenance log used prebuilt 8zqr binaries including empty_16_1_1_64_1_1.out (grid 16x64). That build directory is not in the tree; building the divergent_branch family regenerates the baseline as grid 4x64, which is what this arm uses.
substituted_input.consequence: The RATE of negative null readings is baseline- and run-dependent: the prebuilt 16x64 pair gave 10/20 in the provenance log, this arm measured 3/20 in one run at the old tip and 7/20 at this tip. The SIGN defect is present in every run; the exact count is not reproducible and is not asserted.

reading.finding: The shipped median estimator returns a NEGATIVE kernel_us for a cell that is the same binary as its own floor, so a negative reading is the estimator's noise and carries no information about the kernel. The warm-min floor removes nearly all of them; the real tiny kernel stays non-negative.
reading.not_claimed: No claim that any specific row's kernel_us is correct, no change to the admission threshold, and the negative is never clamped to 0 (7m60's flagging stays the safety net).

gate: cited in the submission comment; no gate is claimed here
